abertura: This is the calendar entry for the call in your lesson.

doc.titulo: Q2 people numbers -- São Paulo sites
doc.texto:
When: Thursday, 5:00–5:30 p.m. (São Paulo)
With: Renata (HR), Greg (Finance), Alison (Operations, US)
Agenda: turnover by site · cost estimate

abertura: Mark the **two** things this entry does **not** tell you.

itens.t: Which sites the numbers cover
itens.porque: The title says it: the São Paulo sites.

itens.t: Whether anything will be decided on the call
itens.porque: Nothing in the entry says a decision is expected. The agenda only lists numbers.

itens.t: Who will be on the call
itens.porque: Three names, each with a department.

itens.t: Which country Alison works in
itens.porque: It is in brackets next to her name: Operations, US.

itens.t: What questions the directors will ask
itens.porque: No calendar entry says that, and it is the part nobody can prepare for completely.

itens.t: What the agenda is
itens.porque: Two items: turnover by site, and a cost estimate.

sec1.rationale: The entry says who, when and what about. It says nothing about decisions or questions, which is where most calls go somewhere nobody planned.

abertura: Choose the better meaning for each expression. All six are said in the call.

itens.t: an exit
alts: the door out of a building

itens.t: to get up to speed
alts: to learn enough to do a new job well
to work faster than the others
itens.ok: to learn enough to do a new job well

itens.t: a recruiting fee
alts: what a new employee pays to apply
what a company pays to find a new person
itens.ok: what a company pays to find a new person

itens.t: lost productivity
alts: work that does not get done while a position is empty or someone is still learning
itens.ok: work that does not get done while a position is empty or someone is still learning

itens.t: a line in the budget
alts: a cost shown separately in the budget
the limit of what can be spent
itens.ok: a cost shown separately in the budget

itens.t: to bring a number down
alts: to present a number to the board

abertura: A colleague leaves Renata a voice message before the call. Listen once, without stopping.

audio.texto: Hi Renata, this is Paula from finance. I am putting the slides together for Thursday. On the turnover slide, the number for Sorocaba says thirteen percent, but your note says thirty. Can you tell me which one is right before the call? Thanks.

abertura: Mark the **one** sentence that says what Paula wants.

itens.t: She wants to move the call to another day.
itens.porque: The call is still on Thursday. She is preparing the slides for it.

itens.t: She wants Renata to present the slides.
itens.porque: She is putting the slides together herself. She needs one number checked.

itens.t: She wants to know which of two numbers is correct.
itens.porque: The slide says thirteen and the note says thirty, and she asks which one is right.

itens.t: She wants the cost of turnover at Sorocaba.
itens.porque: She talks about the turnover number, not about cost.

sec3.rationale: One thing: two numbers that sound almost the same, and one of them is wrong.

abertura: Now a site update, with five numbers in it. Listen for the **numbers** and what each one belongs to. You can listen at the slower speed.

audio.texto: At Sorocaba, fifteen people left in April, and fifty in the first half of the year. In the packing area, overtime went from thirteen to thirty hours a week. At the smaller site it stayed at fourteen.

itens.t: Weekly overtime in the packing area now
itens.porque: From thirteen to thirty. In thirty the stress is at the start: THIR-ty.

itens.t: People who left Sorocaba in April
itens.porque: In fifteen the stress is at the end, and the final n is clear: fif-TEEN.

itens.t: Weekly overtime at the smaller site
itens.porque: It stayed at fourteen, stress at the end. Forty is not said anywhere.

itens.t: People who left in the first half of the year
itens.porque: Fifty in the first half of the year: FIF-ty, stress at the start.

itens.t: Weekly overtime in the packing area before
itens.porque: The first number after from: thir-TEEN.

sec4.rationale: Four of the five come in pairs that sound alike. The stress tells them apart: -TEEN at the end, -ty at the start.

nota.texto: Fifteen and fifty differ in one sound and in where the stress falls. In a fast call the stress is usually what you can still hear.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. All five are ways to ask for a number again on a call.

itens.t: Sorry, was that
alts: fifteen or fifty did you say?
itens.porque: Was that is already the question: the two numbers come straight after it.

itens.t: Could you say
alts: the last figure one more time again?
itens.porque: The thing you want, and then again at the end.

itens.t: Just to check,
alts: was per month, not per year?
that was per month, not per year?
itens.ok: that was per month, not per year?
itens.porque: A statement with a question mark: you say what you understood and let them confirm it.

itens.t: Did you
itens.porque: After did the verb stays in the base form: say. Adding the digits, one three, removes the doubt.

itens.t: Sorry, I did not
itens.porque: After did not the verb stays in the base form: catch. Catch is the usual verb for hearing a number or a name in time.

sec6.titulo: After the number, back to the update
abertura: Complete each sentence. You can use these sentences on a call, and in your lesson.
itens: "Sorry, I {missed} the second number. Could you say it again?"
"{Let me} think about that for a second."
"So, {going back} to the numbers, turnover at the second site is lower."

itens.t: Turnover at Guarulhos went up to 14.6%.
itens.porque: Renata: “voluntary turnover went from nine point two to fourteen point six percent.”

itens.t: Most of the cost appears as one line in the budget.
itens.porque: The opposite: “Most of it is lost productivity, so you won’t see it as one line in the budget.”

itens.t: Renata gives Greg a cost per exit that the company actually paid.
itens.porque: It is an estimate: “We use an estimate of about four thousand eight hundred seventy dollars per exit.”

itens.t: Forty-eight people left in three months.
itens.porque: “That’s forty-eight people who left in three months.”

itens.t: Greg wants to know how the total was calculated.
itens.porque: Renata asks whether he means the total or how they get to it, and Greg says: “How you get to it.”

itens.t: Renata has already decided on a new shift model.
itens.porque: She asks for “a decision on the shift model before the end of the month.” Nothing has been decided.

tf4.rationale: Two figures, one question about method, and three statements that sound likely and are not what anyone says.

opcoes: to find out what someone needs

itens.t: "Is that money we actually spent, or money we lost?"
itens.porque: Greg offers two options and wants Renata to say which one it is.

itens.t: "Was that fourteen or forty?"
itens.porque: Alison did not catch the number. Renata answers with the number and the digits: “One four.”

itens.t: "What would you need from us to bring it down?"
itens.ok: to find out what someone needs
itens.porque: Alison is asking for a request from HR, not for more analysis. Renata answers with one thing: a decision on the shift model.

itens.t: "Do you mean the total, or how we get to the total?"
itens.porque: Renata’s own question. She gives Greg two meanings of his question and lets him choose.

itens.t: "Can you break that down for me?"
itens.porque: Greg wants an explanation, and the question can point to two different ones. That is why Renata checks before answering.

qw4.rationale: Five questions, four different jobs. The one that can go wrong is break that down: an answer to the wrong meaning sounds like a dodge.

What you are doing
Checking what a question means before you answer it, and asking for a number again when you did not catch it.

Key vocabulary
an exit · to get up to speed · a recruiting fee · lost productivity · to bring a number down

callout.titulo: The move that saved the answer
callout.texto: Greg asked Renata to break the cost down. She named the two things he could mean and let him choose. Her answer was then the one he wanted, and she had a few seconds to think.
